dedupe_keys.name: pakistan modelling municipal solid waste emissions and nature based solution scenarios

description: This case study models the municipal solid waste sector with Pakistan as its focus, estimating its climate and ecosystem impact and testing waste diversion scenarios. The authors, researchers at Government College University Lahore, the Urban Unit, the University of Huddersfield and Pakistani government bodies, published it in an open-access journal article. They calculated an ecological impact value for the waste sector across world regions and built scenarios of waste diversion and related emissions, including nature-based solutions at disposal sites. Coverage is national for Pakistan with regional comparisons. The article is free to read under a Creative Commons Attribution licence. Caveats: the scenarios rest on aggregate generation and collection figures, and the article gives limited detail on model inputs. The study reported that only 78 percent of municipal solid waste is collected, that the waste sector's ecological impact value exceeds 50 percent in Africa, Asia, Latin America and the Caribbean, that business as usual attributes 3.42 percent of global emissions to waste, and that two of its diversion scenarios would let regions reach zero carbon in the sector, with low-cost nature-based solutions reducing emissions from disposal sites. Simulation uses: scenario inputs for waste sector emissions and climate adaptation planning. Related records: the What a Waste global database (data-what-a-waste-global-database) supplies country waste statistics, and the IPCC waste model (model-ipcc-waste-model-first-order-decay) estimates landfill emissions.
